A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniEdit-Flow, with matching core algorithms and identifiable retained experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and editing evaluations, hyperparameter studies, and qualitative image/video results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds component ablations, iterative-inversion comparisons, and experiments with image-conditioning and control plugins.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged, but Appendix G substantially extends the pipeline's inputs and components. IP-Adapter and InstantCharacter introduce source/reference-image conditioning, while ControlNet introduces spatial control through modified velocity functions in Equations G.20–G.21.

E1.justification: v2 adds reference-image style transfer, reference-character face editing, and GTAV driving-scene environment editing constrained by segmentation-derived edges. These introduce new conditioning requirements and application coverage. Sketch/stroke generation and video editing already appeared in v1 and are retained.

E2.justification: The existing benchmark comparator sets remain intact. New Table D.3 adds GNRI and ReNoise to direct inversion/reconstruction comparisons; ReNoise previously appeared in the diffusion editing comparison, but not this inversion comparison.

E3.justification: Editing evaluation gains background LPIPS and MSE metrics. New protocols include controlled component ablations, inversion comparisons on 500 CC3M images using 50 diffusion or four SDXL-Turbo steps, and plugin-specific settings. The sketch/stroke delay setting also changes from '0.8 or 1' to 0.8, without establishing that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained delay/guidance sensitivity plots, v2 adds Table C.1 and Figures C.1/C.3 testing inversion, correction, velocity fusion, and regional masks. Figure 4 also adds Uni-Inv error curves. These directly examine component necessity, editing failures, background damage, and overexposure.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The signed parenthetical values in v2 Table C.1 are differences from the full method, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Matching earlier scores are retained, while v2 adds editing metrics, component-ablation results, inversion comparisons, error curves, and plugin demonstrations. For example, new Table D.3 reports unconditional SDXL-Turbo PSNR of 20.08 for Uni-Inv, 17.59 for ReNoise, and 13.46 for GNRI. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1, its assumptions and Appendix A proof, the Appendix B guidance derivation, and the existing sampler formulations are retained. The expanded implicit-Euler explanation and plugin-conditioning formulas do not introduce a new theoretical result or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: accurate inversion, region-aware editing, model independence, and low inference cost. Added experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds an implicit-Euler interpretation and component-specific explanations of editing strength, background preservation, fusion benefits, and overexposure. Appendix G discusses broader plugin-based applicability, but Appendix J retains the earlier image-text-only limitation without reconciling it with the new image-conditioned demonstrations.

D1.justification: Appendices D.3 and G add concrete implementation information: baseline optimization settings, plugin checkpoints, application-specific hyperparameters, null-text conditioning, and Canny extraction from segmentation labels. Existing pseudocode, principal experimental settings, and the project-page link remain available.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including FlowEdit, TweezeEdit, GNRI, InstantCharacter, and GTAV, and discusses connections to plugin-based conditioning. The main research-positioning argument remains intact; bibliographic updates and consolidated FLUX references do not constitute new positioning.

P1.justification: Section 4 receives explanatory and notation refinements, Applications moves from Section 5.4 to Appendix F, and the appendices gain a contents page and additional subsections. Author information, acknowledgements, and an LLM-use statement are updated or added, while most existing narrative is retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to the ICLR single-column format, with widespread repositioning of figures and tables. Figure 4 is expanded, Figure 5 is redrawn, editing tables gain metric columns, and new ablation tables, comparison tables, and application figures are added. Earlier qualitative galleries are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical justification of the central method: Table C.1 and Figure C.3 address v1's lack of direct component ablations, while Table D.3 adds relevant iterative-inversion comparisons and editing tables broaden quality measurement. The plugin experiments also substantiate wider applicability. These gains outweigh the unresolved inconsistency between Appendix G's image-conditioned demonstrations and Appendix J's retained limitation; the new applications remain supported primarily by qualitative examples.
